shots.ring: leopard (tan base, dark brown and black spots all around)
shots.still: Image 1 is the product reference sheet of the real 7 rings. Image 2 is a close-up of the real leopard ring: its colour and print must match image 2 colour for colour. Image 3 is Grace's real bare hands. Image 4 is the room. Close-up at hand height in a bright bedroom (image 4): her right thumb and index finger pinch the leopard ring at the top of the frame, squeezing it slightly into an oval to show it is soft. The ring is a plain ThunderFit silicone band: 5.5 mm wide, 2 mm thick, rounded dome outside, smooth matte silicone, about the width of a fingernail's tip, a solid ring is one flat colour all the way round and a printed ring has its print all the way round the outer band, no stone, no metal, no text, no logo, no shine spots. Grace's hand matches image 3 exactly: medium-brown skin with lighter palms, medium-length squoval nails with mauve-pink polish and white French tips, no other rings, no bracelet, no watch. The hand enters from the frame edge with the whole wrist visible, nothing shows through the hand. Vertical 9:16 phone photo, bright neutral daylight, true colours, no yellow or dark grade, no text, no captions, no logos.
shots.clip: Recreate image 1 exactly as the first frame, then her thumb and index finger squeeze the ring a little harder so the soft band bends into a tighter oval, then let it spring back round. The camera holds still with a slight handheld drift. Image 2 is the real leopard ring: it keeps its exact colour, print, width and size in every frame and never changes shape except where it is pinched. Image 3 is the reference sheet of the real rings. The hand keeps one grip and never swaps hands. Bright neutral light. No music, no voice, no text.
